full_judgment:
Mr. Gour Gopal Saha, J: This rule is directed against the order dated 23.7.98 passed by the Subordinate Judge, 5th Court, Dhaka allowing Miscellaneous Case No. 53 of 1997 under Order 9 Rule 13 of the Code of Civil Procedure setting aside the ex parte decree passed in Title Suit No, 46 of 1997 of Court of the Subordinate Judge and Commercial Court No. 1, Dhaka. 

 2. Short facts relevant for the purpose of the case are that Abdul Khaleque Munshi, the predecessor-in-interest of the petitioners, as plaintiff instituted a suit for declaration of title in the suit property and for a declaration that the proceedings before the concerned Revenue Officer are illegal and without jurisdiction in the 4th Court of the Subordinate Judge, Dhaka being Title Suit No. 383 of 1983, contending inter alia that the suit property appertaining to C.S. khatian No. 107 in C.S. Plot 565 comprising an area of 80.68 acres in mouza Tejkunipara within P.S. Keraniganj, now Gulshan, Dhaka originally belonged to Bhawal Raj Court of Wards Estate the S. khattari urordingly pareas in the name of Kumai Rabindra Narayan Roy Chowdhury. As the laid was a marshy land under deep water it was recorded in the C.S. khatian as 'Beel Bhumr. Abdul Khaleque Munshi being the neighboring owner of some other land started filling earth at his own cost during the years 1927-1936 as a result of which land became fit for cultivation and he grew boro paddy therein. It has been stated that the Bhawal Raj Court of Wards Estate having found Abdul Khaleque Munshi and his benamders in possession of the suit land demanded rent from Abdul Khaleque Munshi and he agreed to pay rent whereupon between 1936-1947, the Bhawal Raj Court of Wards Estate settled 52.17 acres of land by different pattan names on different dates and prepared C.S. B khatian in the name of Abdul Khaleque Munshi and his benamdars and realised rent from them by entering their names in the Tenants' Register No. II, showing the area of land settled and the rate of jama and other charges but Abdul Khaleque Munshi refused to pay rent to the Bhawal. Raj Court of Wards Estate as owner of 28.51 acres of land on the ground that he had been possessing the same on the basis of adverse possession by making it fit for cultivation at his own cost and exertions. As Torab and others illegally cut and took away boro paddy grown by him, Abdul Khaleque Munshi filed a criminal case against those trespassers under section 145 of the Code of Criminal Procedure. The learned SDO and the appellate Court found the said Abdul Khaleque Munshi in possession of 80.68 acres of land and restrained the trespassers by way of injunction from entering into the case land. Thereafter Torab Ali and 91 others filed a suit for declaration of title against Abdul Khaleque Munshi in the 1st Court of the Subordinate Judge, Dhaka being Title Suit No. 89 of 1962. In the said suit the learned Subordinate Judge found Abdul Khaleque Munshi and Amiruddin as borgaders under the Bhawal Raj Court of Wards Estate. Being aggrieved by the aforesaid judgment, Abdul Khaleque Munshi and Amiruddin filed Title Appeal No. 134 of 1964 in the Court of the District Judge, Dhaka and the learned Additional District Judge, who heard the said appeal, allowed the appeal and set aside the judgment of the trial court on the finding that Abdul Khaleque Munshi and Amiruddin have right title, interest and possession in the land of CS Plot No. 565. Being aggrieved by the aforesaid judgment, Abdul Khaleque Munshi, son of Abdul Hakim, Torab Ali and 90 others filed Second Appeal No. 685 of 1970 before the High Court Division but the said appeal was also dismissed and the judgment and decree passed in Title Appeal No. 134 of 1964 were affirmed. Against the aforesaid judgment of the High Court Division, Abdul Khaleque Munshi , Son of Abdul Hakim and 91 others, who were the plaintiffs of Title Suit No. 89 of 1962, filed CPLA No 84 of 1974 before the Appellate Division but were unsuccessful. Eventually 14.16 acres of land out of the aforesaid 80.68 acres of land in CS Plot No. 565 was acquired by the Rajuk in Land Acquisition Case No. 55 of 1958-59 and compensation was assessed in the name of Abdul Khaleque Munshi and his benamder Amiruddin. As the compensation assessed by the Collector was inadequate, plaintiffs Abdul Khaleque Munshi and Amiruddin filed Arbitration Case No. 248 of 1966 before the District Judge, Dhaka who ultimately assessed compensation at Tk. 347760/00 in place of Tk. 46368/00 as assessed by the Collector. Against the aforesaid judgment and order the Government filed 2nd Appeal No. 169 of 1970, which was subsequently converted into Civil Revision No. 807 of 1993 before the High Court Division, to reduce the amount of compensation. The Government thus recognized and accepted the title of the plaintiff Abdul Khaleque Munshi in the suit land. In the meantime, RS operation in respect of the land of 80.68 acres along with other lands started. In the Bujarat stage of RS operation plaintiff Abdul Khaleque Munshi got the land of 80.68 acres recorded in his name and in the name of his benamder and transferees but at the attestation stage the Government and other persons, including the principal defendants, filed a dispute case claiming title in 80.68 acres of land. Most of the defendants are either the heirs and heiresses or transferees of the 92 plaintiffs of Title Suit No. 89 of 1962 in the 1st. Court of the Subordinate Judge, Dhaka. It was alleged that not only the defendants have got no legal claim or title in the suit land but also their claim is barred by the principle of resjudicata in view of the decision in the aforesaid Title Suit No. 89 of 1962 and Title Appeal No. 134 of 1964. It has been further alleged that the settlement officer of the basis of some false and fabricated documents and in deference to the decision of Title Suit No. 89 of 1962, Title Appeal No. 134 of 1964 and Second Appeal No. 685 of 1970 and CPLA No. 84 of 1974, recognised the claim of the defendants and illegally passed order for recording the names of the defendants in the RS khatian in respect of 80.68 acres of land, including 17.3067 acres in the name of transposed plaintiff Nos. 2-12 as shown in schedule 'B' and .4164 acres of land in the name of pro-forma defendant No. 128 as shown in schedule 'C' to the plaint. The land measuring 1.4750 acres out of 52.17 acres has not been recorded the name of pro-forma defendant Nos. 129 and 130, and it has been wrongly shown as vest-ed property. It has been further alleged that no land having vested in the Government, it cannot claim any title thereto. The defendants have no right, title, interest and possession in the suit land measuring 80.68 acres and the claim of the defendants and the orders of the settlement officials during the RS operation recording the suit land in the names of the defendants are wrong and hence the suit for declaration of title in the suit land. 

 3. Abdul Gafur and Hafizuddin appeared in the suit by filing power on 19.4.84 in Title Suit No. 383 of 1983 before ale of Subordinate Judge, Dhaka and prayed for time for filing written statement. Thereafter the suit was transferred to the 1st Court of the Subordinate Judge, Dhaka for expeditious disposal of the suit and was renumbered as Title Suit No. 83 of 1985. The said  Abdul Gafur and Hafizuddin, being defendant Nos. 20-25, sought for adjournments for filing written statement in the suit but ultimately they did not file any written statement within a period of 10 years. Ultimately their application for adjournment for filing written statement was rejected by the Court on 14.8.94. Thereafter the Chairman and the Manager of the Bhawal Raj Court of Wards Estate filed an application under Order 1 Rule 10 of the Code of Civil Procedure for being added as a defendant in the suit and the said prayer was allowed by order dated 11.3.97 whereby the Chairman and the Manager of the Bhawal Raj Court of Wards Estate were made defendant Nos. 131-132. These defendants subsequently filed written statement in the suit denying all material allegations of the plaint and contended inter alia that the suit property belonged to Bhawal Raj Court of Wards Estate. The suit was ultimately transferred from the 1st. Court of Subordinate Judge, Dhaka to the Subordinate Judge and Commercial Court No. 1, Dhaka by order dated 27.3.97 and the suit was renumbered as Title Suit No. 46 of 1997. In course of time 3.4.97 was fixed for peremptory hearing of the suit and it was eventually decreed on 19.5.97 on contest against defendants Nos. 131 and 132 and ex parte against the rest, excluding the present petitioners. 

 4. Thereafter defendant Nos. 20-25 filed an application before the subordinate Judge and commercial court No. 1, Dhaka under Order 9 Rule 13 of the Code of Civil Procedure for setting aside the ex parte decree dated 5.11.94 whereupon Misc. Case No. 10 of 1997 was started. The learned District Judge, Dhaka thereafter transferred the said Misc. Case No. 10 of 1992 to the Subordinate (Judge, 5th Court, Dhaka where it was renumbered as Misc. Case No. 53 of 1997. 

 5. The plaintiff resisted the aforesaid Misc. Case by filing written objection denying all its material allegations and contended inter alia that the defendants were never pre-vented by sufficient cause from appearing before the court when the case was called on for hearing. It was further contended that the story of illness of the learned Advocate for the petitioners and of the petitioner No. 1 himself is false and fabricated and as such they are not entitled to any relief in the application under Order 9 Rule 13 of the Code of Civil Procedure. 

 8. Being aggrieved by the aforesaid impugned order dated 23.7.98 allowing Misc. Case No. 53 of 1997 under Order 9 Rule 13 of the Code of Civil Procedure, the petitioners moved this court and obtained the present Rule. 

 9. Mr. Md. Shafiqul Islam, the learned Advocate appearing for the petitioners, submits that in view of the fact that the petitioners of Misc. Case No. 53 of 1997 failed to prove that they were prevented by sufficient cause within the meaning of Order 9 Rule 13 of the Code of Civil Procedure from appearing before the court when the ex parte decree was passed, the learned Subordinate Judge erred in law in allowing Misc. Case under Order 9 Rule 13 of the Code of Civil Procedure on illegal and irrelevant considerations and the same has occasioned failure of justice. The learned Advocate further submits that payment of compensatory cost amounting to Tk. 15000/- cannot be a justification for allowing the application under Order 9 Rule 13 of the Code of Civil Procedure and as such the learned Subordinate Judge was manifestly wrong in not dismissing the case as the petitioners failed to prove that they were prevented by sufficient cause within the meaning of Order 9 Rule 13 of the Code of Civil Procedure and the same has occasioned failure of justice. 

 10. Mr. Khandaker Mahbubuddin Ahmed, the learned Advocate appearing for opposite party Nos. 1-4, on the other hand, submits that the learned Subordinate Judge on careful consideration of the facts and circumstances of the case and the evidence on record on being satisfied about prevention of the petitioners by sufficient cause exercised his judicial discretion in allowing Misc. Case No. 53 of 1997 with a cost of Tk. 15000/00 to the plaintiffs and as such the impugned order does not suffer from any illegality or legal infirmity occasioning failure of justice so as to justify interference by this court exercising revisional power under section 115(I) of the Code of Civil Procedure. 

 11. Mr. Md. Shafiqul Islam, the learned Advocate for the petitioners, submits that although a different view from the one taken by the learned trial court can be taken on the question of sufficient cause, a court of revision will not be justified in reversing the decision of the trial court without finding the order of the trial court illegal and occasioning failure of justice and consequently the impugned order calls for no interference by this court. 

 12. The learned Advocate for the opposite parties submits that in view of the fact that Title Suit No. 83 of 1985 was transferred from the 1st Court of Subordinate Judge to the Court of the Subordinate Judge and Commercial Court No. 1, Dhaka on 23.7.98, which was an off date, beyond the knowledge of the petitioners and their engaged Advocate, they had no scope to know about the development of the proceedings of the suit before the court of the Subordinate Judge and Commercial Court No. 1, Dhaka, where it was renumbered as Title Suit No. 46 of 1997 and this non-notified transfer must be considered as a sufficient cause preventing the petitioners from appearing before the court when the impugned ex parte order was passed and in that view of the matter the impugned order was rightly set aside by the learned Subordinate Judge on cogent ground and it suffers from no illegality to call for interference in revision. Mr. Ahmed further submits that in view of the fact that a compensatory cost of Tk. 15000/- has been allowed to the plaintiffs towards mitigating their financial losses by exercising sound judicial discretion by the learned trial Court and proper justice has been meted out to the parties, the impugned order has not occasioned failure of justice that may call for interference by this court. 

 13. The learned Advocate appearing for the petitioners has placed before us the impugned order as well as an application under Order 9 Rule 13 of the Code of Civil Procedure and written objection filed thereto. The learned Advocate has placed before us the material evidence adduced by the con-tending parties in Misc. Case No. 53 of 1997. It appears that the learned Subordinate Judge on detailed discussion of the facts and circumstances of the case and the evidence on record found, as of fact, that the petitioners were prevented by sufficient cause from appearing before the court when the impugned ex parte decree was passed against them. As a safeguard against any prejudice to the plaintiffs the learned Subordinate Judge allowed compensatory cost of Tk. 15000/00 to the plaintiffs as a solatium. This does not in any way come in conflict with the finding of the learned Subordinate Judge that the petitioners were prevented by sufficient cause from appearing when the impugned decree was passed. 

 14. In support of his submissions Nil-. Ahmed has placed before us the case of MA. Wahab and another Vs. Abul Kalam and another, reported in 44 DLR (Al)), 13 wherein it has been held that if an order of the Court affecting one of the pillars of the suit is meant for communication to all parties concerned, it must be communicated before further progress of the suit. In our case under review, it is clearly found that Title Suit No. 383 of 1983 of the 1st Court of Subordinate Judge was transferred to the Court of Subordinate Judge and Commercial Court No. 1, Dhaka on an off date beyond the knowledge of the petitioners and the fact of such transfer was never-brought to the knowledge of either the petitioners or their engaged Advocate so as to give them the opportunity to pursue their cause before the transferee Court. Transfer of a suit from one court to another Court is a very important matter affecting one of the pillars of the suit and that cannot, in all. fairness, be done on an off date keeping the interested par-ties in the dark about it and that too without bringing it to the notice of the engaged Advocates of the parties at any point of time. This transfer of the suit has indeed prejudiced the petitioners seriously and this along should be construed as a sufficient cause within the meaning of Order 9 Rule 13 of the Code of Civil Procedure preventing the opposite party petitioners from appearing before the court when the ex parte decree was passed. In support of his contention Mr. Ahmed has placed before me the case of Muhammad Ramjan Sawdagar Vs. AHM Fazlul Huq, reported in 15 DLR, 99 in which a Division Bench of this Court took the view that if an order is passed on an off date, in a case not appearing in the cause list or on a date not fixed for the case, it is incumbent upon° the Court to see that the order is communicated to the engaged Advocate of the concerned parties and when this is not done, the subsequent proceedings must be set aside. Rule 466(2) of the High Court Civil Rules and Order provides that orders directing anything to be done by parties or their pleaders shall be signed by the parties or their Advocates. If further provides that if on an off date an order is passed, endeavors must be made to get it signed by the concerned Advocates before the matter proceeds further. We get instant support to our view in the case of Jahurannessa Vs. Safed Ali Bepari and others, reported in 36 DLR. 253. 

 15. In the facts and circumstances of the case, it must be held that the entire exercise by way of transfer of the case to the 1st Court of the Subordinate Judge and Commercial Court No. 1, was made illegally beyond the knowledge and comprehension of the petitioners, opening the gate to the ex parte decree causing serious prejudice to them. The transfer of the case on an off date beyond the knowledge of the petitioners, in the facts and circumstances of the case, smacks of malafides on the part of the plaintiffs to steal a walk over against the petitioners and the question of malafide appears in the fact of the record. 

 18. In the result, the Rule is discharged without any order as to cost and the impugned order dated 23.7.98 passed by the learned 5th Court of Subordinate Judge, Dhaka allowing Misc. Case No. 53 of 1997 under Order 9 Rule 13 of the Code of Civil Procedure is affirmed. 

 19. The order of stay granted earlier by this Court stands vacated. 

 20. Communicate the order to the learned Subordinate Judge, 5th Court, Dhaka at once for his information and necessary action.
